cross_project_obligations.summary: Align watcher thresholds with runtime-core lease expiry handling.
Introduce ecosystem-wide per-cycle latency obligations for budget diagnostics.

unresolved_ideas.summary: Confirm whether shared rate snapshots can drive cross-repo throttling policy without starvation.

topics.title: Watcher-driven cycle release
topics.recommendation_summary: Assume watcher thresholds can gate cycle release while preserving worker autonomy.
tradeoffs: Incorrect timeout tuning can reset healthy workers.
Signal fan-in adds operational complexity in exchange for lower idle cycles.

topics.title: Rate-limit-aware scheduling
topics.recommendation_summary: Assume profile-level quotas can shape scheduling without starving critical work.
tradeoffs: Aggressive throttling can delay high-priority fixes.
Conservative throttling can waste available budget windows.

open_questions: Which watcher threshold values minimize false resets under mixed workloads?
Should throttling policy prioritize recency or impact when budgets are tight?

evidence_refs.notes: Cycle telemetry from canary execution lanes.
Profile budget observations used for scheduling assumptions.

recommendations.summary: Gate cycle release through watcher signals before fallback timeout reset.
recommendations.rationale: This keeps cycle execution deterministic while preserving autonomous worker throughput.
recommendations.expected_impact: Lower idle redispatches and better schedule continuity under variable worker latency.

recommendations.summary: Reserve budget-aware execution lanes for high-impact fixes when quotas tighten.
recommendations.rationale: This protects critical work while still applying profile-level throttle safety.
recommendations.expected_impact: Reduced starvation of urgent fixes during constrained rate windows.
